scope: User-authorized live PostgreSQL multi-connection verification: two different new request IDs retry the same content of an existing committed unresolved reservation. No provider calls, game edits or committed test billing changes.

method.baseline: Read one existing reserved charge. Keep user, project, digest and original request identity inside SQL; export only hashes and assertion results. Do not create or modify the original reservation.
method.connections: Two independent SQL Editor requests execute BEGIN ... ROLLBACK. Each invokes the actual deployed beegame_image_billing with a distinct new request ID, the same original content digest, amount=1 micro-Credit and budget=1 micro-Credit. The unresolved-reservation branch must return before new reservation or budget accounting.
method.overlapProof: After its RPC returns, connection A keeps the transaction-level wallet advisory lock. It checks pg_stat_activity with refreshed statistics until connection B is active and waiting on an advisory lock, and pg_blocking_pids(B) includes A. After observing this, A waits one second and rolls back. B then returns its receipt and rolls back. Missing overlap or changed baseline causes an exception, not a pass.
method.timeouts: statement_timeout=30s, lock_timeout=12s, idle_in_transaction_session_timeout=35s; A waits at most 20s for proven overlap.
method.rollback: Both complete SQL batches end in ROLLBACK. An independent read-only transaction subsequently verifies unchanged wallet/project-ledger hashes, no new request rows, no remaining test transaction and no advisory locks for either backend.

boundaries.note: This proves concurrent renamed retries against an existing committed unresolved reservation. It is not a test of two first-ever requests with no existing reservation, an HTTP generation-route test, or a stress/load test.
